'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***The [[governor of Luhansk Oblast]], [[Serhiy Haidai]], reports that all hospitals in the province have been completely destroyed by the [[Russian Armed Forces]]. Russia denies the claim, accusing Ukraine of destroying their own hospitals. [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/ukraine-russia-putin-news-04-07-22/h_f3c7feb54a77b20bad830cf1eb44be94 (CNN)]
***Mayor [[Borys Filatov]] requests that all women, children, and elderly leave the city of [[Dnipro]] in preparation for a possible [[Russia]]n attack. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2022/apr/07/russia-ukraine-war-nato-foreign-ministers-to-meet-as-zelenskiy-dismisses-fresh-sanctions-live-news?page=with:block-624edbde8f083703c7bd7a32#block-624edbde8f083703c7bd7a32 (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[2022 Tel Aviv shooting]]
***Three people are killed and 11 more are injured during a [[mass shooting]] at a bar in [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]]. The attacker is killed during a shootout in nearby [[Jaffa]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-61021186 (BBC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[Boycott of Russia and Belarus]]
***The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes 420–3 to pass legislation to suspend normal trade relations with [[Russia]] and [[Belarus]] following the invasion of [[Ukraine]]. Following this, the [[United States Senate|Senate]] also votes 100–0 to pass the legislation, sending it to [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] for approval. [https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/Alert-Congress-OKs-bills-suspending-normal-trade-17064497.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')] [https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/senate-vote-suspend-russia-belarus-normal-trade-relations (Fox Business)]
**The [[Russian ruble]] goes above the pre-[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|war]] level after falling as low as 150 rubles per US dollar in early March. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-04-06/mocked-as-rubble-by-biden-russia-s-ruble-comes-roaring-back?srnd=premium-europe (Bloomberg)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Eight people are killed and three more injured during an explosion at a bar in a military camp in [[Goma]], [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. The causes of the blast are unknown. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/explosion-bar-kills-eight-congolese-military-camp-2022-04-07/ (Reuters)]
*Around two million people in [[Puerto Rico]] are [[Power outage|left without electricity]] after a fire occurs at one of the island's largest [[power plant]]s. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/puerto-rico-plunged-into-darkness-after-power-station-fire/2022/04/06/04f084b4-b619-11ec-8358-20aa16355fb4_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*A [[DHL Aviation|DHL]] [[Boeing 757-200]] [[cargo plane]] breaks into two parts after making an [[emergency landing]] at the [[Juan Santamaría International Airport]] in [[San José, Costa Rica]]. No one is injured. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/costa-ricas-main-international-airport-remain-closed-most-day-after-emergency-2022-04-07/ (Reuters)]
*At least 11 people are killed and a dozen injured in a [[landslide]] in [[Abriaquí]] municipality, [[Colombia]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/04/07/americas/colombia-landslide-miners-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus]]
***[[Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Cyprus]] will lift their [[COVID-19]]-related travel conditions from April 18, ending rules of two years of the pandemic. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/cyprus-lift-covid-19-travel-conditions-april-18-2022-04-07/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan]]
***[[Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Kazakhstan]] will lift their [[COVID-19]] travel restrictions at the country's borders with [[Kyrgyzstan]], [[Russia]] and [[Uzbekistan]]. [https://astanatimes.com/2022/04/kazakhstan-to-lift-restrictions-at-border-checkpoints-with-kyrgyzstan-russia-and-uzbekistan-next-week/ (''Astana Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
****[[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Nancy Pelosi]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/04/07/us/politics/nancy-pelosi-covid-positive.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[Government and intergovernmental reactions to the Russian invasion of Ukraine|International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***The [[Eleventh emergency special session of the United Nations General Assembly|emergency special session of the United Nations General Assembly]] votes to suspend Russia from the [[United Nations Human Rights Council|Human Rights Council]], with 93 votes in favor, 24 against and 58 abstentions. Russia is the second country to be suspended from the council, after [[Libya]] in 2011 during [[First Libyan Civil War|the final year]] of [[Muammar Gaddafi]]'s [[History of Libya under Muammar Gaddafi|rule]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/ukraine-russia-putin-news-04-07-22/h_80a4549d20246240a97c27645b46f953 (CNN)]
**[[Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***[[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] says that [[Government of Belarus|Minsk]] should be included in negotiations aimed at ending the war. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2022/04/07/belarusian-president-demands-role-in-talks-on-ukraine-war-a77262 (''The Moscow Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**Former German [[Federal Ministry of Justice (Germany)|Justice Minister]] [[Sabine Leutheusser-Schnarrenberger]] and former [[Federal Ministry of the Interior and Community|Interior Minister]] [[Gerhart Baum]] file a complaint with German federal [[prosecutor]]s accusing [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]], all 32 members of the [[Security Council of Russia]], and members of the [[Russian Armed Forces]] of committing war crimes in Ukraine. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/german-officials-file-war-crimes-complaint-russia-83928381 (ABC News)]
*An unknown assailant throws [[acetone]] and red paint at [[Russians|Russian]] [[Nobel Prize laureate]] [[Dmitry Muratov]] as he traveled on a [[Moscow]]–[[Samara]] train, injuring him. A motive for the attack is unknown, but it is suspected to be a possible reaction to Muratov's opposition to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. [https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-new-novaya-gazeta-europe-muratov/31791421.html (Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-nobel-peace-laureate-muratov-says-he-was-attacked-with-red-paint-2022-04-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[March–April 2022 Peruvian protests|2022 Peruvian protests]]
**The [[Government of Peru|government of Pedro Castillo]] announces that they have deployed the [[Peruvian Army]] to highways amid protests against [[inflation]] in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-deploys-army-highways-blockades-continue-2022-04-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[Ketanji Brown Jackson]] is confirmed for the [[Supreme Court of the United States]], following a 53–47 vote by the [[United States Senate|Senate]]. Jackson is the first [[Black people|black]] woman to be confirmed for this position and will replace justice [[Stephen Breyer]] after he retires in the court's summer session. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2022/04/07/us/ketanji-brown-jackson-vote-scotus (''The New York Times'')]
*[[President of Yemen]] [[Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi]] resigns from office, dismisses [[Vice President of Yemen|vice president]] [[Ali Mohsen al-Ahmar]] and transfers both office's powers to the newly formed eight member [[Presidential Leadership Council]] chaired by [[Rashad al-Alimi]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-61020866 (BBC News)]
'''Science and technology'''
*It is announced that over 5,000 new species of previously undiscovered [[RNA viruses]] were found in [[ocean]]-living organisms and proposed to group them into five new [[Phylum|phyla]], according to a paper published in ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/undiscovered-viruses-oceans-tara-study-b2053513.html (''The Independent'')]
